newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's July industrial output fell 0.92 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's July industrial output fell 0.92 pct.

text.p: Colombia's industrial production, excluding coffee processing, fell 0.92 percent in July over the same month last year, the National Statistics Department (DANE) said.

It said the drop, the first on record for the month this decade, contributed to a 0.49 percent fall in industrial output during the first seven months of 1996 versus the same period last year. Including coffee processing, industrial production increased 0.47 percent in the seven-month period.
Employment in the manufacturing sector has dropped 2.94 percent so far this year, according to DANE.
The negative growth, excluding coffee processing, in industrial activity in July comes against the backdrop of a sharp economic slowdown so far this year.
High interest rates, Colombia's prolonged political crisis, and a deep slump in the construction sector have all been blamed by leading business groups for flagging growth in industry.
A recent surge in leftist guerrilla activity has also been cited as a factor adversely affecting the manufacturing sector.

A recent drop in interest rates, which fell five percent in August, could help breathe new life into the sector in the fourth-quarter. But analysts say growth expectations remain limited. -- Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944
